::: {#exm-population-sample-wcgs}
#### Population and sample in the WCGS

In 1960, the WCGS recruited employed men aged 39 to 59 years in California.
Take that group of men as the study's population (@def-population),
so the population distribution (@def-population-distribution) of cholesterol is its distribution among those men.
The `wcgs` data frame is the sample (@def-sample):
it holds `r nrow(wcgs)` of the men in that population.
The men volunteered, through 10 companies,
so the sample is not a random sample (@def-random-sample) of the population.
Its mean cholesterol, `r round(mean(wcgs$chol, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` mg/dL,
describes these `r nrow(wcgs)` men exactly,
but it estimates the population mean well
only to the extent that the volunteers resemble the rest of the population.
:::
